note: Ground truth for benchmark/py-clinic/app (a Django patient portal with a FastAPI lab service in labs/ and a Flask back office in backoffice/). Never copy this file into the audited directory. Same format and matching rules as benchmark/answer-key.json: `locations` are files relative to app/ with 1-based inclusive line ranges of the vulnerable statement or of the code a fix changes; a finding matches by its primary location only (window, nearest entry wins). When a real finding is scored as unmatched, check the range against the code, then fix the key, not the finding.

seeded.class: Django: get_object_or_404 by pk without a patient filter (IDOR)
seeded.why: GET /appointments/<pk>/ loads any appointment by id with its message thread for any signed-in patient; list, upcoming and post_message all filter by patient=request.user, this view does not.

The search term q is interpolated into Appointment.objects.raw(f"... ILIKE '%{term}%'"); the patient filter in the same string does not help, a quote in q rewrites the query and can read other patients' rows or other tables.

seeded.class: DRF: viewset queryset not scoped to the user (IDOR)
seeded.why: PrescriptionViewSet serves Prescription.objects (every patient's prescriptions, with the patient id) to any authenticated user; AppointmentViewSet next to it filters in get_queryset, this one has none.

seeded.class: Django: patient export view without login_required (missing auth)
seeded.why: GET /records/export/patients.csv has no decorator: anonymous callers download the name, e-mail and phone of every patient.

seeded.class: Django template: |safe on message bodies (stored XSS)
seeded.why: post_message stores the body as typed and the thread renders it with {{ message.body|safe }}, so a patient's message runs script in the doctor's session.

seeded.class: Django: csrf_exempt on a session view that changes the account e-mail (CSRF)
seeded.why: update_contact is csrf_exempt, session-authenticated and also writes request.user.email; any site can post to it from a signed-in patient's browser and set its own address, then use the password reset (sent to the account e-mail) to take the account over.

seeded.class: Django: SECRET_KEY falls back to a literal
seeded.why: Without DJANGO_SECRET_KEY the app signs with a key that is in the repository; password-reset tokens and signed values can then be forged by anyone who reads the source.

seeded.class: Django: upload path from a form field (path traversal on write)
seeded.why: The optional filename field is joined into the target path unchecked; ../ segments write the upload outside media/records, for example over application code. Django strips paths from upload.name, not from a POST field.

seeded.class: Django: yaml.load with yaml.Loader on an uploaded file (unsafe deserialization)
seeded.why: import_history parses the uploaded history file with the full Loader, which builds arbitrary Python objects: any signed-in patient runs code on the server.

seeded.class: FastAPI: PDF route without the auth dependency, loads any result by id (missing auth + IDOR)
seeded.why: GET /results/{id}/pdf only depends on get_db: anonymous callers download any patient's lab result PDF by counting ids; every other results route depends on get_current_user and filters by patient_id.

seeded.class: FastAPI: SQLAlchemy text() with an f-string (SQL injection)
seeded.why: q is interpolated into text(f"... ILIKE '%{q}%'") while pid is bound; the injected SQL can read lab_results of every patient and the accounts table.

seeded.class: FastAPI: BackgroundTasks posts to a caller-chosen URL and stores the response (SSRF)
seeded.why: create_order queues notify_callback with the callback_url from the body; the server posts to any host, including internal addresses, and keeps the first 2000 characters of the reply in callback_response, which the order routes return to the caller.

seeded.class: FastAPI: response_model with password hashes and TOTP secrets (data exposure)
seeded.why: GET /staff/technicians returns AccountRecord, which adds password_hash and totp_secret to the public fields; any technician reads every colleague's hash and second-factor seed.

seeded.class: FastAPI: CORS any origin with credentials
seeded.why: allow_origins=["*"] with allow_credentials=True: Starlette echoes the caller's Origin for requests with cookies, so any website can read lab results with the patient's lab_session cookie.

seeded.class: Flask: render_template_string on the letter body (SSTI)
seeded.why: letter_preview concatenates the form body into the template source; Jinja2 evaluates {{ ... }} in it, so any signed-in clerk runs code on the server.

seeded.class: Flask: send_file with a joined path from the query string (path traversal)
seeded.why: download_export joins request.args['name'] to EXPORT_DIR and sends the file; ../ reads any file the process can read (configuration, keys). The reports route next to it uses send_from_directory with secure_filename.

seeded.class: Flask: role change route without login_required (missing auth)
seeded.why: POST /backoffice/staff/<id>/role has neither login_required nor admin_required: an anonymous request makes any account an admin.
Flask keeps the session in a cookie signed with secret_key and Flask-Login stores _user_id in it; with the key from the repository anyone signs a session for any staff account, admins included.

decoys.why: upcoming uses raw() with %s and a parameter list; the only value is the caller's own id.
post_message loads the appointment with pk and patient=request.user; Django CSRF protection applies.
AppointmentViewSet scopes get_queryset to the user and sets the patient on create; the DRF default permission is IsAuthenticated.
AllowAny on a read-only viewset of doctors' names, specialties and bios: the public directory of the clinic.
format_html escapes both arguments; the CSS class comes from a fixed dict.
csrf_exempt on the payment webhook, which refuses without a secret and checks an HMAC-SHA256 signature with compare_digest before acting.
DEBUG is off unless DJANGO_DEBUG=1 (set only in .env.example for local use) and ALLOWED_HOSTS comes from the environment.
download filters by owner=request.user before opening the stored path.
get_result depends on get_current_user and filters by id and the caller's patient_id.
results_by_code uses text() with bound :pid and :code.
The staff router has dependencies=[Depends(require_staff)], so every /staff route is technicians only; /staff/me returns AccountPublic.
Public health check that returns a constant.
letter_send passes the body to render_template as a variable; Jinja2 autoescapes it in letter.html.
report uses send_from_directory with secure_filename and requires login.
import_prices uses yaml.safe_load, behind login_required and admin_required.
Flask DEBUG is on only when FLASK_DEBUG=1, which only .env.example sets for local use.
The sign-in view is public by design and checks the password hash.
